gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the TerraMaster F2-425 Plus's Intel N150 iGPU delivers 24 EU × 1.0 GHz = 24 EU·GHz of shader throughput for $399.49 ($16.65 per EU·GHz), 33% more than the UGREEN DXP2800's N100 (24 EU × 0.75 GHz = 18 EU·GHz, $389.99, $21.67 per EU·GHz) for a $9.50 price gap, with Synology's J4125 models at 12 EU × 0.75 GHz = 9 EU·GHz.
standout_why: Compared against starryhope.com (prices, Plex Pass 3-year cost, idle watts for DXP4800 Plus/DXP6800 Pro only; no per-CPU iGPU figures), nasdecoded.com (no prices, no numbers), terabytewise.com (Quick Sync yes/no only), datacenterdisk.com (prices and core counts only), computingforgeeks.com (yearly electricity cost from TerraMaster/UGREEN rated watts at $0.20/kWh, so the power-cost derivation is already partly covered) and ChatGPT's own answer (unverified 'estimated 2–4 streams' table). None of them derive iGPU execution units × clock from Intel ARK or price per unit of iGPU throughput, which is the hardware budget that decides HDR tone-mapped 4K transcodes. It is not a 3 because no named reviewer has published measured simultaneous 4K HEVC transcode counts for any of these exact NAS units, so the proxy cannot be converted to a cost-per-stream figure.
decides: Confirms the F2-425 Plus over the DXP2800 as the pick: for $9.50 more it buys 33% more iGPU shader clock on the same 24-EU layout (plus a third NVMe slot and dual 5GbE), and it rules out the Synology J4125 units (DS225+, DS425+) on hardware alone: half the execution units of the N100/N150 at the same 750 MHz, before the DSM iGPU-driver removal already noted on our page. The Asustor AS5402T's N5105 sits between them (19.2 EU·GHz) but at a higher Amazon price than either, so it stays a runner-up.

findings.label: Derived: iGPU shader budget (EUs × max graphics clock)
findings.source_title: Intel ARK spec pages (N150, N5105, N100, J4125 as cited above)
findings.note: 24 × 1.0 = 24.0; 24 × 0.8 = 19.2; 24 × 0.75 = 18.0; 12 × 0.75 = 9.0. Method: the fixed-function Quick Sync decode/encode block is shared across these parts, but Plex's HDR-to-SDR tone mapping and scaling run as shaders on the execution units, so EU count × clock is the hardware headroom for tone-mapped 4K transcodes. It is a proxy, not a measured stream count.
